To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a large fraction of LIP neurons are modulated by visual attention, and that the majority of these neurons also are modulated by the active limb.

a large fraction of neurons in the LIP of rhesus macaques encode the location of an attended visual target and that a fraction of them simultaneously encode the identity of the limb that is to be moved.

the lateral intraparietal area (LIP), a brain area implicated in visual attention, is involved in visuospatially guided movements of the hand, and that LIP neurons encode both visuospatial information and the active limb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that allow the brain to integrate information from the senses and from the body.
the neural mechanisms of visual perception, attention, and action

the neural basis of attention, which is the process by which a subset of information is selected from an environment for further processing, and the neural basis of eye movements, which is the rapid movement of the eyes to foveate objects of interest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LIP is a part of an attentional system that is involved in the selection of behaviorally relevant visual stimuli for action, including saccadic and limb movements.
LIP is a key structure for visuospatial selection and action, and that it is involved in the coordination of visual and motor selection in a wide variety of circumstances.
the LIP is a part of a system that integrates visuospatial and effector information in order to select and prepare the appropriate motor response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LIP is a key area for the integration of visuospatial and motor information during goal-directed or symbolicaly cued movements.
the lateral intraparital area (LIP), an area that was initially discovered to be involved in saccadic eye movements, also contributes to the control of limb movements.
LIP integrates visuospatial and effector information during symbolically cued limb movements in monkeys.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LIP is a key structure in the brain for integrating visual information with motor commands.
a single brain area can be involved in multiple functions.
the LIP is a key node in the neural network that links visual information to motor variables.
